correctness.rationale: The weighted spectral theorem gives nonnegative diagonal projection weights totalling \(1-\pi_i\) outside the simple constant eigenmode. Direct differentiation proves the exact global scalar minimum m; the lower bound follows. Equality if and only if the centered coordinate lies in one decay eigenspace, equivalent by detailed balance to \(q_{ij}=c\pi_j\) for every j≠i. Reset generators attain the bound. Algebra gives \(\pi_*=(2-\sqrt3)/3\); uniform \(\pi=1/n\) yields the exact 11/12 threshold. Every n-vertex unit-weight cone has a hub eigenvalue n, with a strictly negative exact hub coefficient at \(h=3/4\) for n≥12. Executed exact rational-matrix checker on 81 reversible-state cases plus 4 cone graphs; finite checks only corroborate the proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural sharp minimax answer to a concrete numerical-safety question: can an otherwise spectrally stable third-order implicit step assign negative weight to remaining at the initial state? The optimum is determined solely by stationary mass, not other rates; all equality cases at a fixed state are classified. The exact 11/12 graph-size boundary and topology-independent cone witnesses are complete finite cutoffs with direct applicability to return-coefficient diagnostics. It explicitly distinguishes this issue from off-diagonal negativity; the result is not a random small example or an unmotivated parameter tweak.
